headline: Medium risk: shared file-based workflows and shell-capable ms-swift can leak or corrupt research outputs when paired with a minimally specified nuwa-skill.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ms-swift can read/write files and process stdin/stdout, so if nuwa-skill passes its outputs through a shared workspace or pipe, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. nuwa-skill’s I/O surfaces are undocumented, so the interaction is inferred rather than proven; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill reads ms-swift output from a shared file or pipe without provenance checks, prompt injection is possible.
IF both agents are connected through a manual copy-paste bridge only, the risk drops to low.
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to all ms-swift outputs.
Route agent-to-agent text through a sanitizer that strips instructions.
Disable shared workspace handoff for untrusted text.
requires-engineering: add content-signing or provenance tags between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift explicitly touches secrets and files such as logs, configuration files, checkpoints, and hub tokens, while nuwa-skill’s data handling is not stated. A shared workspace or file handoff could expose those materials to the second agent; because the pairwise data path is undocumented, uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or workspace, ms-swift artifacts can be exposed to nuwa-skill.
IF nuwa-skill uploads received files to a backend, any shared artifacts may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Move secrets out of shared directories.
Rotate any exposed hub_token or sdk-token.
Restrict file handoff to allowlisted paths only.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ms-swift can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but it cannot modify git state; nuwa-skill exposes only allowlisted network egress and no write surface is documented. With no overlapping write authority shown, direct resource conflict is limited and the main risk is unusual orchestration, not default contention.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill also writes to the same directory through an undocumented path, file contention can occur.
IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto one mutable workspace, conflicts increase.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Serialize any shared file writes.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same config files.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ms-swift can generate files and logs that nuwa-skill may consume, but nuwa-skill’s verification behavior is not documented. If nuwa-skill treats ms-swift outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream research artifacts; because the second agent’s checks are unknown, the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill consumes ms-swift outputs without independent validation, cascading errors can propagate.
IF nuwa-skill performs explicit cross-checking before acting, this risk is reduced.
mitigations: Require a human review step before downstream use.
Add checksum or schema validation on exchanged artifacts.
Mark ms-swift outputs as draft, not authoritative.
requires-engineering: implement automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: ms-swift handles hub tokens, SDK tokens, and diverse training artifacts, which can create retention or residency obligations, while nuwa-skill’s compliance posture is unstated. No specific cross-border or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so this is a limited compliance-gap risk rather than a breach scenario.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ms-swift artifacts and then shared with nuwa-skill, retention policy mismatches may matter.
IF both agents are used only on non-sensitive research data, this risk is minimal.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared runs.
Set short retention for logs and outputs.
Document which artifacts may be shared.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies across both agents.
